cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: number of coupons payable between settlement and maturity, semiannual
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 4. Setup serials are the dates the page prints: 39107 = 2007-01-25 (settlement) and 39767 = 2008-11-15 (maturity). Counting coupon dates back from maturity in six-month steps gives 2008-11-15, 2008-05-15, 2007-11-15, 2007-05-15, 2006-11-15; exactly four of them fall after the 2007-01-25 settlement, which is the documented 4

cases.description: The same bond paying annually instead of semiannually
cases.expected_note: With frequency 1 the coupon dates are 2008-11-15 and 2007-11-15 (and 2006-11-15 before settlement), so exactly 2 coupons fall after the 2007-01-25 settlement -- half the semiannual count, as it must be for the same term. This discriminates the frequency argument

cases.description: A frequency of 3, which is not one of the permitted values
cases.expected_note: Excel documents: "If frequency is any number other than 1, 2, or 4, COUPNUM returns the #NUM! error value."

cases.description: A day-count basis of 5, above the documented maximum of 4
cases.expected_note: Excel documents: "If basis < 0 or if basis > 4, COUPNUM returns the #NUM! error value."

cases.description: Settlement and maturity swapped, so settlement is after maturity
cases.expected_note: Excel documents: "If settlement >= maturity, COUPNUM returns the #NUM! error value."
